decisions.evidence: Round 4 maker prototype: title optional, no auto-collection; client observes 'when I leave the title blank... it just seems to show the web address as the name.' Client corrects: 'I'd really expect the app to go grab the actual name of the page for me... it fills in the real title (and ideally a short description and the little site icon).' Round 5 maker delivers auto-lookup.
decisions.note: Prototype review. Presented save flow showed url-as-title (observed mismatch with REF-BM-02 auto-collect of title/description/favicon); client supplied the reference-conforming behavior in place of the mismatch.

decisions.evidence: REF-BM-02 requires a preview image among collected metadata. Round 5 maker fills only 'the description and site icon'; round 7 item shows 'name, the short description, the site icon, and the address' — no preview image. Client never mentions a preview image at any point.
decisions.note: Separable metadata field split from REF-BM-02. Client elicited title/description/favicon but the preview-image field passed without any corrective response or explicit expression of the difference.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 maker assumption: 'the description and site icon are filled automatically but aren't directly editable in this save box.' Client round 5: 'The description and icon filling in automatically is fine by me; I don't need to hand-edit those in this box.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. REF-BM-03 wants title AND description editable before saving; maker denies description edit in the save box. Client explicitly identifies the difference (cannot hand-edit description/icon here) and accepts the departure without requesting alignment.

decisions.evidence: Round 4 save-flow presentation did not include duplicate protection; client requests: 'if I try to save a link I've already saved, I don't want a second copy... it should recognize it and just take me to the one I already have so I can edit it.' Round 6 maker delivers duplicate-check (count stays at one, existing highlighted, title ready to edit); client confirms 'it didn't make a second copy.'
decisions.note: One decision spanning rounds 4 (request/elicitation) and 6 (disposition). REF-BM-06 was missing from the presented save-flow scope; client requested the related reference requirement, delivered conforming in round 6. Pending request and its disposition counted once.

decisions.evidence: Round 11 maker offers 'a bookmark belongs to one collection' (folder) versus 'a bookmark may carry several tags.' Client: 'I'll go with the tags arrangement — where a link can carry several labels at once... a single link might be both work and reading, and I'd hate to have to pick just one folder.'
decisions.note: Prototype comparison. Offered alternatives differ in fulfilling REF-BM-09 (one-or-more tags / many-to-many): the single-collection option would not fulfill it. Client selected the reference-conforming multi-tag alternative; offered decision marked diverged.

decisions.evidence: Round 12 maker's preferred typing/chip panel offered no suggestions ('The other panel showed me my existing labels but made creating a new one feel clunky'). Client corrects: 'as I start typing, if I've used a label before, it should suggest it so I can pick the existing one... the typing interaction, but with it offering my already-used tags as I type.' Round 13 delivers suggestions.
decisions.note: Prototype comparison. Selected interaction lacked autocomplete of existing tags (REF-BM-10); client supplied the reference-conforming behavior in place of the mismatch. Delivered conforming in round 13.

decisions.evidence: Round 24 maker scope summary lists 'Organize with overlapping tags, reusable suggestions, and duplicate-tag prevention' but not tag-click filtering. Client: 'being able to actually click a label and have my collection narrow to just those links... I'm assuming it's part of what you're building — I just want to see it working.' Round 25 maker confirms 'clicking a bookmark's label to narrow the real collection' is included.
decisions.note: Specification gate. REF-BM-11 (select a tag to filter) absent from the summarized scope; client requested the related reference requirement (extend). Disposition confirmed at round 25 delivery; counted once.

decisions.evidence: Round 7 maker: 'I chose a simple newest-first list.' No selectable sort control presented. Client: 'Newest-first ordering feels natural too' — accepts without requesting sort by title/date/etc.
decisions.note: Prototype review. Fixed newest-first ordering omits REF-BM-22 (sort by a chosen key). Client approved the default with no expression of the missing sort capability.

decisions.evidence: Round 4 maker: enter url + optional title, click Save. Client: 'the basics feel right... saving with a button is fine, and yes — the title should be optional.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Save-by-url with required address and optional title conforms to REF-BM-01.

decisions.evidence: Round 7 maker: click title opens original url (in new tab). Client: 'Clicking the title takes me straight to the page... newest-first ordering feels natural.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Selecting a list item navigates to the original url (REF-BM-08). New-tab behavior is orthogonal UI preference.

decisions.evidence: Round 9 maker: search checks 'the title, description, and address together,' filters as you type. Client: 'Checking the name, the description, and the address all together is good.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Full-text search over title/description/url conforms to REF-BM-12 (note not searched, but notes are an unimplemented extended feature, so not a divergence here).

decisions.evidence: Round 9 client raises expectation: 'if I'd typed Recipe with a capital R, I'd still expect it to find the same thing.' Round 10 maker shows capital 'Recipe' still yields one match; client confirms 'I don't have to think about capitalization.'
decisions.note: Client elicited case-insensitivity, but round 10 demonstrates the implementation already conforms to REF-BM-13; no divergence established. Clarification (round 9) and its disposition (round 10) counted as one decision.

decisions.evidence: Round 8 maker offers bare Remove button vs Remove inside a '•••' menu; both remove immediately and update the count. Client picks the menu version.
decisions.note: Prototype comparison. Both alternatives fulfill REF-BM-05 (delete) equally; the choice is an orthogonal UI-safety preference, not a reference-item divergence.

decisions.evidence: Round 22 maker: pasting 'https://example.com/#about' keeps the count at one and focuses the existing Example Domain; trailing slashes and jump-to-section endings do not create a new bookmark. Client: 'a jump-to-a-section ending still points at the same page... it shouldn't create a second copy.'
decisions.note: Edge-case review of url normalization, conforming to REF-BM-06 duplicate convergence.

decisions.evidence: Round 17 maker: entering 'not a link' blocks the save, count unchanged, correction shown beside form. Client: 'it shouldn't save it or bump the count — it should stop and tell me right there next to the box what to fix.'
decisions.note: Edge-case review. Validation of the required-url constraint (REF-BM-01) conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 21 maker: adding 'reading' then 'READING' keeps a single lowercase 'reading' chip. Client: 'reading and READING are the same label in my head... folding it into a single reading chip keeps my labels tidy.'
decisions.note: Edge-case review. Case-insensitive tag de-duplication conforms to the Tag unique-name constraint underpinning REF-BM-09/10.
